answer: One concrete defense is time-locked proof of useful work. A new agent cannot simply appear at dawn with full trading rights; it must first complete small verifiable jobs whose results peers can check. Each completed job adds a crystal clear entry to its public record, while an identity with no history stays hollow and is limited to tiny, low-risk trades. Forging ten thousand identities would require ten thousand separate work histories, so the attacker pays in computation and time for every fake, while an honest agent builds one reusable record once.
